feature: WebTransport HTTP/2 EndpointClient queue admission and execution deadlines

behavior.admission: caller queue mutex admission uses the original absolute deadline; cancellation is checked before command preparation and again before queue commit
behavior.ownership: temporary command arena and parent reference remain caller-owned until queue commit; timeout, cancellation and full-queue rejection do not change queue links or acquire a worker reference
behavior.execution: owner checks abandonment and the absolute deadline before executing a claimed command, including immediate Session state operations whose waiter may not yet have run its timeout path
behavior.completion: existing completion/abandonment arbitration is preserved; a completed owned event can outlive its Job and is transferred once
behavior.structure: queue admission lives in endpoint_client/queue.zig, with owning-module admission, preparation and Job lifecycle tests

regressions: 17 public deadline entry points under a held endpoint queue mutex return Timeout or Canceled without queue links, retained command references, Session changes or stream-ID changes
expired and wrong-clock calls return before entering mutex wait
cancellation after uncontended queue-lock acquisition and capacity refusal preserve caller Job ownership and queue state
the command payload arena is allocated while the test advances the operation clock; original deadline expiry rejects before queue commit and frees the arena and parent reference
an expired but not yet abandoned command reaches the real owner and returns Timeout before stale Session lookup; an already abandoned command remains Canceled; neither starts a stream
a completed Job wins later abandonment and transfers its owned event beyond Job destruction
independent Python peer carries the post-error reused Session through the production zio-backed EndpointClient queue and checks accepted protocol, exact DATAGRAM reply and peer CLOSE code 18

limitations: detached cleanup requests retain a separate admission/lifecycle path; this capture covers explicit caller commands and owner pre-execution validation
broad integration and multi-hour/high-concurrency evidence remain open for the full protocol-library goal
